pl-l3d39c8-d1e115.summary: Asks whether one may use the faith of someone who swore by demons or idols.

pl-l3d39c8-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine to Publicola: whoever swears by false gods and does not keep faith sins twice, swearing by whom he should not and breaking his promise. Whoever uses for good the faith of one who swore by false gods does not join his sin but his good pact of keeping faith. It is less evil to swear truly by false gods than falsely by the true God, since the holier what is sworn by, the more punishable the perjury.
claims: Using another's oath by false gods for good is not sharing his sin.
Swearing truly by false gods is less evil than swearing falsely by the true God.
Perjury is graver the holier what is sworn by.

pl-l3d39c8.summary: Asks whether one may make use of the good faith of someone who swore by demons or idols. Augustine to Publicola: one who swears by false gods and breaks faith sins twice. Whoever uses for good the faith of one who swore by false gods joins not in his sin of swearing by demons but in his good pact of keeping faith. It is less evil to swear truly by false gods than falsely by the true God, for the holier what one swears by, the more punishable the perjury.
claims: Swearing by false gods and breaking faith is a double sin.
One may use for good the faith of one who swore by false gods.
Swearing truly by false gods is less evil than swearing falsely by the true God.
Perjury is graver the holier what is sworn by.
